subject: Decision Making
subcategory: Famous Decisions That Changed the World
title: Ford Pays $5 a Day
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Ford Pays $5 a Day.

hook.text: In 1914, Henry Ford doubled worker wages to $5 a day. Competitors called him insane. Workers lined up for miles.

buildup.text: Ford's assembly line was efficient but brutal. Worker turnover was 370 percent per year.

discovery.text: Higher wages cut turnover dramatically. Workers stayed, got skilled, and produced more. The math worked.

twist.text: Ford's workers could now afford to buy the cars they built. He accidentally created his own customer base.

climax.text: Ford's decision shows that paying more can cost less. Counterintuitive logic sometimes outperforms conventional wisdom.

punchline.text: Double the wage, halve the costs. Counterintuitive moves can win.

quiz.question: Why did Ford's wage increase actually save money?
options: Dramatically lower turnover reduced training costs and boosted productivity
